learn.title: 17 · Reference solution

designClaim: walk one root-to-leaf path, going the way the target points and keeping the closest value seen — O(h)
solutionMd:
## The idea

The BST order means you never need both sides. At each node, remember it if it is closer than the best so far, then go **left if the target is smaller, right if larger**. One path from root to leaf.

## Step by step

1. best = root value.
2. At each node: if closer (or equally close and smaller), update best.
3. Go left if target < value, else right.
4. Return best.

## Worked example

**Input:** BST [4,2,5,1,3], target 3.714286

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| at 4 | distance 0.29 → best 4; target < 4 → left |
| at 2 | distance 1.71 → keep 4; go right |
| at 3 | distance 0.71 → keep 4 |
| end | no child |

**Result:** 4

## Cost

O(h) time, O(1) memory.

## The code (C#, compiled and tested against every part of the question)

```csharp
// TreeNode is provided by the starter (Models.cs): int Value; TreeNode Left, Right.

// LeetCode 270 — the value in a BST closest to a target. On a tie, the smaller value.
public static class ClosestBst {
    public static int Value(TreeNode root, double target) {
        if (root == null) throw new ArgumentException("empty tree");
        int best = root.Value;
        TreeNode cur = root;
        while (cur != null) {
            double d = Math.Abs(cur.Value - target), bd = Math.Abs(best - target);
            if (d < bd || (d == bd && cur.Value < best)) best = cur.Value;
            cur = target < cur.Value ? cur.Left : cur.Right;   // the BST order says which side can be closer
        }
        return best;
    }
}
```
